newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS FIRMER ON QUIET DAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS FIRMER ON QUIET DAY.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar closed firmer on Monday against most hard currencies after a fairly quiet interbank session, dealers said.

Some dealers added they were baffled that the local unit had continued strong over the past week, against a depreciatory trend in the last quarter of the year when importer demand for foreign currency outweighs export supply in the southern African country.
"I think what could be sustaining the dollar are off-shore loans that some clients got and also everyone now has faith that the Reserve Bank won't let the dollar go wild," one dealer hazarded.
The central bank came into the market two weeks ago to restore confidence by selling U.S. dollars after panic buying saw the local unit at on epoint go down 15 cents against the key U.S. unit.
On Monday, the local unit closed at 10.5575/5775 against the U.S. dollar, up from last Friday's 10.5650/5850 and was at 17.2950/3390 from 17.3500/3900 versus pound sterling.
It was also firmer against the rand at 2.2450/2520 compared to 2.2800/3000, but slipped to 6.9740/9920 from 6.9600/9800 against the mark.
